title: metadata-04: recursive depth def, object-only ns values
description:
draft-ietf-jmap-metadata-04 redefines depth and requires namespace values to be objects.

-04 §2.1: "The depth of a value is defined recursively: a scalar (string, number, boolean or null) has depth 0; an array has the maximum depth of its elements (0 if empty); an object has depth 1 plus the maximum depth of its member values (1 if empty)."
-04 §2.1: "The value associated with each namespace key MUST be a JSON object ... a namespace set to {} remains stored until it is removed with null."
-04 §1.2.1 maxDepth: "If not null, the value MUST be at least 1."
(-02: "Scalar values ... and empty arrays or objects have depth 1 at the position they occupy.")

Affected:
- crate-jmap-metadata-server/src/validate.rs:50-52 value_depth returns object_nesting(value).max(1). Under -04 the result is object_nesting (validate.rs:18-24) unclamped: scalars 0, [] 0. For object values the result is unchanged.
- crate-jmap-metadata-server/src/validate.rs:26-49 rustdoc and doctests (value_depth("hello") == 1, etc.) encode the -02 rule.
- crate-jmap-metadata-server/src/validate.rs:123-151 tests depth_scalar_*/depth_empty_array assert 1. That oracle was -02; update to the -04 oracle (scalar 0, [] 0, {} 1).
- -04 says a namespace value that is not an object is invalid. No helper rejects it today. Decide whether exceeds_max_depth/value_depth callers need an is-object check, or document that the caller enforces it.
- crate-jmap-metadata-types/src/capability.rs:66-72 max_depth doc ("Depth 1 = flat properties only..."). Restate it with the -04 definition and note >= 1 when non-null.

value_depth and exceeds_max_depth keep their signatures; the return values change for non-object inputs.
